speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have a psychiatric condition and have developed a new movement disorder; could you please describe the specific movements you are experiencing and when they started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful context. To better evaluate your movement disorder, could you tell me if the movements are rhythmic or jerking, and do they occur in your arms, legs, face, or neck?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient describes symptoms of akathisia, which is a common side effect of risperidone. Have you noticed any muscle stiffness, tremors, or changes in your speech or swallowing? REQUEST TEST: Prolactin, CK.

speaker: Doctor
text: The test results are normal, which helps rule out severe muscle injury or significant hyperprolactinemia. Given your history of risperidone use and symptoms of inner restlessness, have you noticed any worsening of your psychiatric symptoms or any history of similar reactions to other medications?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.
